metadata.study_title: Administrative Coordination and Permitting Delays: An Open-Data-Informed Simulation Study
metadata.diagnostic_reference: Teinemaa, Leontjeva, & Masing (2015), BPIC 2015: Diagnostics of Building Permit Application Process in Dutch Municipalities

collection_totals.timestamp_identifiability_note: Teinemaa et al. (2015, Sec. 2, pp. 3-6) audited eight timestamp attributes and identified extensive missingness in five attributes (dueDate, dateStop, planned, endDatePlanned, and endDate), measuring elapsed intervals using sequential time:timestamp values with three-digit action codes (01_HOOFD_xxx) used to order events within tied timestamp batches. Subtracting time:timestamp from dateFinished also produced negative differences whose recording conventions could not be clarified with the process owner.
collection_totals.provenance: Directly observed in published source (van Dongen 2015; Teinemaa et al. 2015, Sec. 2 & Sec. 6)

M1.organizational_profile: 3 specialized role clusters (admin, regular DM, environmental DM); phase-transfer registration lags

M2.organizational_profile: Generalist roles with high self-loops; extended-case & objection delays; shared staff (560530, 560532) with M5

M3.organizational_profile: Single generalist cluster with frequent inter-resource handoffs; intake confirmation delays

M4.organizational_profile: Strong April/June closure peaks; sign-off bottleneck at resource 560752 in decision irrevocable stage

M5.organizational_profile: High completeness-subcase frequency; hub concentration at resources 560600 and 560602

contextual_bimp_reference.provenance: Published stochastic what-if BIMP simulation in Teinemaa et al. (2015, Sec. 6, Table 5, p. 21), which estimated branching probabilities, fitted exponential phase-duration distributions, and ran three simulations of 2,000 cases for each scenario (modifying both clarification phases and premature termination steps). Used as a contextual comparison, not as an independent validation test or calibration target.

distributional_and_uncertainty_assumptio.phase_holding_time_distributions: Gamma distributions parameterized to preserve exact published Layer A phase means with assumed baseline shape parameters: S1 k=1.0 (exponential fit in Teinemaa et al. 2015 Fig. 16), S2 loop k=2.0, S3 receptive k=1.5, S3 advice k=1.2, S4 concept/draft/decision_ready k=1.5 (draft_made k=1.0), S5 taken/sent k=1.5, S6 irrevocable k=3.0 (end k=1.5)
distributional_and_uncertainty_assumptio.replicate_percentile_range_definition: 95% Replicate-Percentile Range [Rep PR] (2.5th to 97.5th percentile across 30 Monte Carlo replications of N=2,000 cases under fixed baseline parameters), describing finite-batch simulation variability alongside batch-mean standard error SE_batch
distributional_and_uncertainty_assumptio.assumed_input_variation_interval_definit: 95% Assumed-Input Variation Interval {Input VI} across 100 parameter vectors theta_j applying an assumed 12% coefficient of variation (Gamma scaling) to all phase holding-time means, Normal(0.28, 0.03) clipped to [0.18, 0.40] for baseline rework probability, and Normal(3.2, 0.40) clipped to [2.0, 4.5] days for handoff delay
distributional_and_uncertainty_assumptio.matched_input_contrast_design: Within each configuration, B0_baseline, I1_routing_continuity, I2_rework_prevention, and I3_targeted_intake are evaluated across the exact same 100 parameter vectors theta_j (rng_theta = default_rng(cfg_seed + 100000)) and matched trajectory seeds (rng_traj = default_rng(cfg_seed + 200000 + j) and rng_mc = default_rng(cfg_seed + r)), isolating Delta_j = g(I, theta_j) - g(B0, theta_j)
distributional_and_uncertainty_assumptio.provenance: Scenario assumption (distributional shapes and 12% input-perturbation bands are modeling assumptions, not empirically estimated sampling distributions)

complexity_index.provenance: Scenario assumption (normalized operational complexity proxy for required subcases and advice steps)

branching_handoff_and_rework_specificati.first_loop_rework_probability_formula: p_rework_1(C_i) = clip(rework_prob_base + 0.20 * (C_i - 0.50), 0.05, 0.65) when rework is active; 0.0 when disable_rework=True
branching_handoff_and_rework_specificati.second_loop_conditional_prob_formula: p_rework_2_given_1(C_i) = 0.15 * (p_rework_1_eff(C_i) / 0.28), scaling proportionally with effective first-loop rework probability
branching_handoff_and_rework_specificati.advice_step_condition: 1 advice step if C_i >= 0.35; 50% weight additional advice step if C_i > 0.70
branching_handoff_and_rework_specificati.case_level_handoff_delay_draw: Each case i draws a shared case-level per-handoff delay factor d_i ~ Gamma(2.0, eta / 2.0) multiplying its realized handoff count H_i (T_coord,i = H_i * d_i)

C0_no_friction.description: Reference holding times without additional coordination penalties (published BPI 2015 phase holding durations with zero added handoff penalty)

C1_linear_handoff.description: Linear handoff friction where each case's Poisson handoff count H_i is multiplied by a case-level draw d_i ~ Gamma(2, 1.6) days (mean 3.2 d)

C2_threshold_governance.description: Threshold referral regime where intermediate cases (0.35 <= C_i <= 0.70) incur extra specialist referrals while high-tier cases (C_i > 0.70) receive senior case-team coordination scaling S3 and S4 by gamma_high

C3_congestion_rework.imposed_congestion_multiplier_formula: 1.0 + 0.65 * (rho - 1.0) * (1.0 + 0.90 * mean_p_rework_eff), plus 1.12x scaling on S2 rework holding time and 1.10x scaling on handoff delay
C3_congestion_rework.description: Imposed workload-and-rework congestion scenario increasing upper-tail delay relative to the reference comparison via a parametric multiplier (not an empirical estimate of a real 25% arrival increase or an endogenous continuous-time queueing model)

I1_routing_continuity.description: Case-ownership continuity reducing inter-resource handoffs by 60%

I2_rework_prevention.description: Pre-submission digital completeness check reducing clarification rework probability by 50% and rework holding time by 15%

I3_targeted_intake.description: Targeted early intake review for upper-complexity cases (C_i > 0.55, ~42.4% of applications at baseline) reducing their rework probability by 45%, rework duration by 25%, and handoffs by 50%
